title: Bounded quasi-coherent derived limit of an infinitesimal module system
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology. Regard $M_n$ as a module on $X$ by direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$; the given transition isomorphisms followed by quotient maps define its inverse-system maps. The symbol $R\varprojlim_{D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}}M_n$ denotes the homotopy inverse limit in this full derived subcategory: it fits into the product triangle $K\to\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\prod_{n\geq1}M_n\to K[1]$, with products taken in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and projections $q_n:K\to M_n$ induced by the first arrow. Here the shift has $n$th component equal to the transition map composed with the $(n+1)$st projection. These products and this homotopy inverse limit exist. The resulting $K$ belongs to $D^b_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i<0$. Its projections satisfy $q_{n-1}=t_nq_n$, where $t_n:M_n\to M_{n-1}$ is the indicated transition map.

proof.text: The projection $A\to A_n$ is surjective: lift any element of $A_n$ recursively through the surjective transitions for larger indices, and use its images for smaller indices. Thus $i_n:X_n\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact and separated: after a scheme test it is a closed subscheme, whose inverse image of an affine is the spectrum of a quotient; its diagonal is an isomorphism. The quasi-compact separated pushforward theorem makes $i_{n,*}M_n$ quasi-coherent. Its ringed-topos direct image is the specified chart-limit direct image by the chart-limit comparison. From now on write $M_n$ for this module on $X$. The finite-presentation convention in the statement, over the affine base, makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Work on the equivalent small ringed model. Resolve each object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ by a K-injective complex. Sectionwise module limits supply all termwise products; the product-of-K-injectives theorem says that these products represent products in the derived category. In particular $B=\prod_nM_n$ exists in the ambient derived category. The derived-limit existence theorem gives a triangle $L\to B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to L[1]$ there.

Let $I=I_X$ and $DQ=DQ_X$ from the space coherator adjunction. For every $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, the natural equalities $$\operatorname{Hom}(P,DQ B)=\operatorname{Hom}(IP,B)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(IP,M_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(P,M_n)$$ show directly that $DQ B$ is the product in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, its $n$th projection being $DQ(\mathrm{pr}_n)$ followed by the inverse unit $DQ(IM_n)\simeq M_n$. Naturality of this unit identifies $DQ(1-s)$ with one minus the transition shift for these projections. Since $DQ$ is triangulated, its image of the triangle in step 2 is the required product triangle, with first object $DQ L$. Any $K$ specified in the item is isomorphic to $DQ L$ by uniqueness up to isomorphism of derived limits.

For an affine etale $u:U\to X$, tensor pullback $u^*M_n$ is quasi-coherent. On the localized ringed site, sections and derived sections over the object $U$ are global sections and derived global sections of this restriction; this is the localization identification of the enlarged etale ringed model. The ringed-site derived-evaluation/slice comparison identifies the cohomology of $R\Gamma(U,M_n)$ with abelian-sheaf cohomology on that slice. Enough injectives holds by step 2. The scheme Zariski/etale quasi-coherent equivalence realizes $u^*M_n$ as the associated etale sheaf of a quasi-coherent Zariski module. Affine etale acyclicity therefore gives $R\Gamma(U,M_n)\simeq\Gamma(U,M_n)[0]$. The site derived-sections/derived-limit theorem, applied to step 2, identifies $R\Gamma(U,L)$ with a derived limit of the tower $R\Gamma(U,M_n)$.

Apply the Milnor short exact sequence to the tower of abelian-group complexes in step 4. Its stage cohomology is zero except in degree zero. If $i<0$ or $i>1$, both $H^{i-1}(R\Gamma(U,M_n))$ and $H^i(R\Gamma(U,M_n))$ are zero for every $n$. Both outside terms of the Milnor sequence are therefore zero, giving $H^i(U,L)=0$ for $i\notin[0,1]$, uniformly for all affine etale $U\to X$. No Mittag-Leffler assertion or exactness of products of module sheaves is needed.

The space coherator bound applied to $L$, with $a=0$ and $b=1$, gives an integer $N\geq0$ with $H^i(DQ L)=0$ outside $[0,1+N]$. By step 3 the same holds for $K$. Its cohomology is quasi-coherent because it is an object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. Thus $K\in D^b_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and it has no negative cohomology. The extra flatness, finite-presentation, nilpotence and proper-support assumptions on the tower were not used in steps 2--6.

Write the specified product triangle as $K\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\to K[1]$. Consecutive arrows of a distinguished triangle have zero composite, so $(1-s)p=0$. Composing with $\mathrm{pr}_{n-1}$ gives $0=\mathrm{pr}_{n-1}p-t_n\mathrm{pr}_np=q_{n-1}-t_nq_n$. Hence the projections of this very triangle satisfy the required identity; it does not require a canonical choice of derived limit.
